prerequisites: It is recommended to have completed the courses Physics I, Physics II, Calculus, and Algebra.
A review of trigonometry, geometry, vector calculus, and complex numbers is also useful.

learning_outcomes.text: That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their area of study.
Ability to work, lead and manage conflicts in a multidisciplinary group and/or a multilingual environment.
Ability to apply new technologies including information and communication technologies.
Ability to manage information, handle and apply technical specifications and the necessary legislation for engineering practice.
Ability for oral and written transmission of information adapted to the audience.
Knowledge and use of the principles of circuit theory and electrical machines.
Knowledge of the fundamentals of electronics.
Knowledge of the fundamentals of automatisms and control methods.

syllabus_topics: Potential difference between the terminals of a dipole.
Conversion of voltage source to current sources and vice versa.
Analysis of electrical circuits using the mesh method.
Analysis of electrical circuits using the node method.
Topic 4. CIRCUITS IN SINUSOIDAL STEADY STATE
Instantaneous power and active or consumed power.
Phase or simple values and line or compound values.
Topic 6. GENERAL PRINCIPLES OF ELECTRICAL MACHINES
Basic constructive elements: Ferromagnetic core: stator, rotor. Windings.
Energy balance and efficiency. Copper, iron, and mechanical losses.
Equivalent circuit of the real transformer.
Operation under load: Internal voltage drop. Efficiency and regulation.
Starting of the three-phase induction motor.
Behavior of passive elements in alternating current.
Alternating current circuits: Analysis of series and parallel RLC circuits.
teaching_methods: Large group lectures (lectures, exposition of theory and general examples)
Small group classes (exercise solving, practical activities, laboratories)
Collective/individual tutorials (doubt clarification, comments on individual assignments)

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and/or participation in face-to-face and/or virtual activities

assessment_rules: The final grade is a weighted average according to the established percentages. To pass the subject, a minimum score of 5 out of 10 must be obtained in the theoretical knowledge test. It is also mandatory to pass the practicals. A practical recovery session will be held for students who have a single unjustified missed practical.
